title: Almond and cherry cake
subtitle: light almond sponge with glacé cherries
excerpt: Almond and cherry cake is a simple British celebration cake with ground almonds in the batter, giving a moist crumb and a subtle marzipan note alongside the glacé cherries. The cherries need washing and drying before they go in, or they will sink through the batter to the bottom of the tin. Quartering them further reduces their weight and helps them stay suspended.
sourceNotes: British almond and cherry cake tradition (documented in various 19th and 20th-century household baking manuals). Mrs Beeton (Book of Household Management, 1861, public domain). Constance Spry (The Constance Spry Cookery Book, 1956, public domain).

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap in foil and freeze for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake 1 to 2 days ahead; the almond crumb improves with keeping.
recipe.temperatureNote: conventional oven; slow bake for even heat through a dense batter

baking.decoratingTechnique: Flaked almonds scattered on top before baking

recipeTools.notes: 20 cm round tin, greased and lined.

glossaryTerms.definition: Beating softened butter and sugar together until the mixture is pale, light, and fluffy before adding eggs and flour. The process incorporates air into the fat, which helps the cake rise and gives a fine, even crumb. The butter must be genuinely soft for the method to work. Under-creamed butter and sugar produces a dense, heavy sponge.

Cherries that have been preserved in a heavy sugar syrup, giving them a bright colour and a very sweet, sticky coating. In baking, the syrup coating must be rinsed off and the cherries dried thoroughly before use. The syrup is too heavy for the cherries to stay suspended in batter; without washing they sink straight to the base of the tin.

items.prepNote: quartered, rinsed under cold water and dried well on kitchen paper

content.text: Prepare the cherries and the tin
Heat the oven to 160 degrees Celsius (conventional). Grease and line a 20 cm round cake tin with baking paper, lining the sides as well as the base.

Quarter the glacé cherries and place them in a sieve. Rinse under cold running water to remove the syrup coating. Spread on several layers of kitchen paper and pat very dry. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the measured flour to coat lightly, which helps them distribute evenly through the batter.

Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together for 4 to 5 minutes until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. If the mixture looks like it might curdle, add a tablespoon of the flour.
Fold in the self-raising flour and ground almonds with a large spatula until just combined. Add the almond extract and fold through. The batter will be thick.
Fold in the prepared cherries gently, distributing them evenly. Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface. Scatter the flaked almonds over the top.

Bake on the middle shelf for 70 to 80 minutes until the top is golden and the flaked almonds are a deep amber brown, the cake has pulled away from the sides of the tin, and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. Check at 60 minutes; if the top is browning too quickly, lay a sheet of baking paper loosely over the tin.

Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then turn out onto a cooling rack and leave until completely cold. The crumb is fragile when warm. The cake improves on the second day and keeps in an airtight tin for up to 5 days.

attrs.problem: Cherries all sink to the bottom
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding cherries without rinsing and drying them first.
attrs.fix: The syrup coating on unwashed glacé cherries makes them too heavy to stay suspended. Rinse, dry thoroughly, and toss in a little flour before folding into the batter. Also ensure the batter is thick before the cherries go in; a loose batter will not support them.

attrs.problem: Almond extract flavour is too strong
attrs.avoid: Avoid using more than 1 teaspoon of almond extract.
attrs.fix: Almond extract is very potent; 1 teaspoon in this quantity of batter is the upper limit. Reduce to half a teaspoon if you prefer a more subtle background note.

attrs.problem: Centre is still raw after the stated time
attrs.avoid: Avoid testing too early or relying on colour alone.
attrs.fix: The almond content and the dense batter mean this cake takes longer than a plain sponge. Continue baking in 10-minute increments, covering loosely with baking paper to protect the top, until the skewer comes out clean and the cake feels firm when pressed at the centre.
